articles.title: Scooby-Doo: Origins Reveals Cute New Photo of the Live-Action Dog
articles.summary: Netflix announced Sunday that production has officially wrapped in Atlanta on their upcoming series Scooby-Doo: Origins. The streaming service also released a new photo of the titular good boy, which can be seen in the image gallery below.
body: Scooby-Doo: Origins marks the first time a real Great Dane has portrayed the beloved canine member of the Mystery Inc. gang.

“During their final summer at camp, old friends Shaggy and Daphne get embroiled in a haunting mystery surrounding a lonely lost Great Dane puppy that may have been a witness to a supernatural murder,” according to the official synopsis.

“Together with the pragmatic and scientific townie, Velma, and the strange, but ever so handsome new kid, Freddy, they set out to solve the case that is pulling each of them into a creepy nightmare that threatens to expose all of their secrets.”
Scooby-Doo: Origins stars Mckenna Grace as “Daphne Blake,” Tanner Hagen as “Shaggy Rogers,” Abby Ryder Fortson as “Velma Dinkley,” Maxwell Jenkins as “Fred Jones.”

articles.title: Netflix’s Biggest Cyberpunk Series Is Doing Something Completely Different in Season 2
articles.summary: That philosophy comes from new series director Kai Ikarashi, who served as storyboard artist and animation director on season 1’s “Girl on Fire.” His use of light helped make it one of the series’ most visually distinctive and memorable episodes.
body: There is no light at the end of the tunnel in Night City. In Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, light isn’t a symbol of hope at all. It’s just another overwhelming force bearing down on the people who live hard lives in an even harder city.
“Rather than using light as something that connects us to the outside world, I used it as something that blocks it off,” Ikarashi tells Polygon. “I depicted light not as hope, but simply as a force.”

Released in 2022, the original Cyberpunk: Edgerunners combines Studio Trigger’s flashy animation with the oppressive dystopia of CD Projekt Red’s Cyberpunk 2077. The story follows David Martinez (Zach Aguilar), a teenager who installs a powerful military implant called the Sandevistan and joins a crew of mercenaries — only to lose his sense of self as he replaces more and more of his body with cyberware. That arc ultimately transforms his charming but strained love story with netrunner Lucy into a tragic one. The neon-soaked Night City is colorful and exciting, but it’s a brutal place that more often than not consumes anyone who tries to rise above their station.

articles.title: Sony is the Bad Guy of 2026, but it’s Going to Win Anyway
articles.summary: Patch Notes is a weekly newsletter bringing you the best of Polygon, sent on Fridays and published on the site on Sundays. You can subscribe here.
body: It's early September: back to school and back to work for most of us, and for the game industry, back to the business end. It was a long summer, but it's over now. Typically, this is when things get really interesting, especially in video games, where the sprint toward holiday sales may not have quite the same emphasis it did 20 years ago, but is still hardly vestigial. Especially when the looming colossus of Grand Theft Auto 6 moves the finish line forward for everyone else ( except Nintendo ).

In Polygon's fall preview this week, we've been rooting around for stories to sharpen your appetite for the season ahead, from talking to Zach Cregger about his Resident Evil movie to talking to talking to the makers of Ace Combat 8 about the art of video game clouds. And hey, did you remember that Gears of War: E-Day is a thing? For some reason, I keep forgetting.

articles.title: Diablo 4's new season brings back Deckard Cain and all three Prime Evils as the game arrives on Switch 2
articles.summary: Diablo 4 's next season, Season of Hell's Legacy, will go live on 15th September to celebrate the franchise's 30th anniversary and Nintendo Switch 2 debut.
body: At BlizzCon's opening ceremony, developer Blizzard said the season will be a tribute to three decades of Diablo, built around the return of Deckard Cain and a rematch against all three original Prime Evils: Diablo, Baal, and Mephisto.

Cain's spirit returns to warn players that echoes of the three Prime Evils have resurfaced. Each one's holed up in a location familiar to those who've played the earlier games - Tristram Cathedral, Arreat Summit, the Durance of Hate. Beat one and you get a Soul Splinter, which lets you borrow a bit of that demon's power. The catch is that it also makes you more vulnerable to that same demon.

That's not all, either. Nine new Legacy Uniques also join the game permanently, including a returning Stone of Jordan, alongside a batch of enemy encounters called Waking Nightmares that recreate specific moments from Diablo's past.
The new content is slated to go live at 5.30pm UK time on 15th September.

articles.title: We Need More Games Like Echo Weaver
articles.summary: Echo Weaver is a platformer due to arrive next month from Moonlight Kids, known for 2021 hit The Wild at Heart. It’s also a Metroidvania that feels a bit like a roguelite, but with more emphasis on puzzles and hand-crafted stages.
body: The game begins by dropping the player character into an alien environment and setting them free to explore until they either die or run out of time. Whatever they discover, that’s the fruit of a single “cycle.” Then they reappear to attempt some of the same things again in the familiar corridors (stages are handcrafted, not procedurally-generated), while relying on knowledge gleaned from their previous runs. As play progresses, the world they know naturally expands. They find ways to push further in all directions, and to unearth secrets about the mysterious complex that contains them. In the process, they might even learn new things about themselves.
Chris Sumsky, game designer, programmer, and Moonlight Kids co-founder, recalled some of the thinking behind the game’s design, which takes cues from the 2019 indie hit Outer Wilds.

“There are time loop games, of course,” Sumsky told Polygon, “not least of which the very one we were inspired by. There are knowledge-gated games, not many, but they’re gaining popularity. And naturally, there are platformers. Many… many platformers. But we weren’t seeing anyone really combining all these into one.”
points: Echo Weaver is a platformer due to arrive next month from Moonlight Kids, known for 2021 hit The Wild at Heart.
It’s also a Metroidvania that feels a bit like a roguelite, but with more emphasis on puzzles and hand-crafted stages.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Set To End Sony's Historic 11-Year GOTY Run
articles.summary: Reviews of Marvel's Wolverine were published this week, and they're on the lukewarm side. Currently, the Insomniac Games title sits at a middling 78 on Metacritic. Critics found its relentless combat action wears thin and were divided on the strength of its storytelling.
body: This is a below-par result for both Insomniac and publisher Sony, and it means Wolverine is unlikely to score a nomination for Game of the Year at The Game Awards — even in a soft year like this one. Critical sentiment is the strongest barometer of success at The Game Awards, where the jury is mostly composed of international games media. There's never been a game nominated with a Metascore below 80. What’s more, as a licensed game. Wolverine faces an additional hurdle. Properties originating outside games are rarely nominated at The Game Awards, with Insomniac's own Spider-Man games among the rare exceptions.
But Wolverine missing a GOTY nomination would break a remarkable 11-year streak for Sony, which is by far the most successful publisher in Game Awards history.

The first year The Game Awards was held, in 2014, no Sony games were nominated for Game of the Year. (The big PlayStation exclusive that year was Infamous: Second Son — Metacritic rating: 80.) But that is the only time Sony hasn't had at least one game nominated for GOTY.

articles.title: Ashly Burch, voice of Horizon's Aloy and star of Mythic Quest, is currently obsessed with Slay the Spire 2 and thinks videogames have too many stoic characters: 'I want more sh*tty little b*tches'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Ashly Burch's first encounter with PC gaming was playing a Donkey Kong knockoff on a PC her mother had bought to practice typing. But the first PC game that truly resonated with her was LucasArts' Day of the Tentacle: "That was the first time I played a game that I can remember that had a narrative and comedy," she says. "It was one of those things where, when you're younger, you find something that expands your concept of what a thing can be."

Burch came to the world's attention through the online, gaming-themed sketch show Hey Ash, Whatcha Playin', before making her videogame acting debut as Tiny Tina in Borderlands 2. Since then, Burch's roles have included Chloe in Life is Strange, Parvati Holcomb in The Outer Worlds, and Aloy in Guerrilla Games' Horizon series.

articles.title: Upcoming vampire RPG Nighthawks has been removed from Steam search and delisted in certain countries as Valve classifies it Adults Only: 'It's very bad news for us'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Nighthawks, the long-in-development vampire RPG due to be released later this month, is the latest game to run afoul of Steam's increasingly stringent rules regarding adult content. According to publisher Wadjet Eye Games, the game has been labelled 'Adults Only'—causing it to be removed from Steam search and outright delisted in certain countries like Germany—despite claims from both developer and publisher that the RPG's depictions of sex and nudity are very mild.

"We are aware that Steam has classified Nighthawks as an adult game and has excluded it from searches," Wadjet Eye boss Dave Gilbert wrote on Bluesky. "We are working on it. Valve is under the impression that this game is way sexier than it actually is." Gilbert further commented that "Valve is basically treating Nighthawks like a porn game!" in responding to a reply to his initial post.

articles.title: The World of Warcraft "Classic+" rumours were true and it's called World of Warcraft: Forever
articles.summary: Blizzard has officially confirmed World of Warcraft: Forever, the long-rumoured "Classic+" experience.
body: Last week, World of Warcraft fans were obsessing over colours as dataminers pulled hues from Blizzard's website that were labelled under a curious "wow 2" tag, leading many to speculate that this referred to the rumoured World of Warcraft Camelot, or as it's better known, "Classic Plus", much like how Blizzard is now expanding Diablo 2.
Now, following BlizzCon's opening ceremony, it turns out the rumours were pretty much bang on and World of Warcraft: Forever launches globally on 4th November.
If November sounds very far away, worry not; beta access begins this Thursday, 17th September, for anyone who's pre-purchased one of the game's upgrade packs.

A dedicated panel featuring senior game director Ion Hazzikostas, lead Classic designer Tim Jones, lead software engineer Nora Mills, and associate production director Clay Stone went into more detail on the new regions, systems, and design philosophy behind the project.
points: Blizzard has officially confirmed World of Warcraft: Forever, the long-rumoured "Classic+" experience.

articles.title: As an OG Crazy Taxi lover, its new remake might just not be crazy enough
articles.summary: I've played just about every damn iteration of Crazy Taxi there is. My first exposure to it was the PlayStation 2 EyeToy version included in Sega Superstars, which involved me wildly gesticulating and yelling in order to get Axel's attention.
body: Then I spent a fair bit of time behind the wheel in both its Dreamcast and arcade versions—we don't talk about the myriad of mobile travesties—so I was pretty jazzed about the announcement of Crazy Taxi: World Tour. I was promptly un-jazzed by all the generative AI discourse that mired the hours following its reveal trailer, but you know.

Allegedly its use remains firmly in the conceptual stages of development, which I still don't love, but I was determined to not let that cloud my opinion of the game as I sat down to give it a whirl at Gamescom. And honestly? After an hour, I kinda felt like that was all the time I needed with Crazy Taxi: World Tour. As much as I wanted to be sold on a modern-day iteration, I'm just not quite there yet.

My time with the demo popped me behind the wheel as Crazy Taxi poster boy Axel, and dropped me into its thematically-appropriate Germany map. There'll be five cities with the full release, but I imagine most of what I saw in the game's amalgamation of various German cities will be true of the rest of the game.

articles.title: The weird, wonderful world of Miles Buckle, Instagram's parallel universe of video games
articles.summary: Going through Miles Buckle's Instagram feed is like stumbling into a parallel universe where cinema's greats – Lynch, Hitchcock, Fellini, Kubrick – are reimagined in the familiar but distinctly different visual language of video games.
body: For his university degree show last year, Buckle, who studied graphic communication design at Central St. Martin's in London, showed his final project, a short game called Nights Bridge, on a plastic-molded cream-griege desktop computer from the ancient times. "I bought a PC from the 90s off eBay," the 3D artist and animator tells me on a video call. "I took the parts out and put in modern hardware, so the monitor and the tower were like, 30 years old, and it had the keyboard and everything." He remembers all of it being obstinately heavy – it was a click-and-collect pickup situation, and he hauled it all home on foot.

articles.title: StarCraft is back, but it's not the RTS you remember - it's an open-world shooter coming spring 2030
articles.summary: Blizzard's next StarCraft game will be an original open-world shooter and it's coming spring 2030.
body: Revealed at BlizzCon 2026's opening ceremony, it marks the first new standalone StarCraft game in around a decade.

Dan Hay, who previously worked as lead producer on Ubisoft's Far Cry series before joining Blizzard, introduced the project, calling it "something new - an open-world shooter where every step is earned. Not from above, but down on the ground, in the mud, in the fire".
"There's only one thing we can say: it's about damn time," Blizzard teases on its website.

The announcement was accompanied by a brilliantly grim cinematic teaser rather than gameplay, following a Terran recruit called Holt whose deployment ends violently within moments of touching down on the Zerg-infested battlefield. Though not confirmed, it sounds as though Arcturus Mengsk is broadcasting throughout the trailer.
points: Blizzard's next StarCraft game will be an original open-world shooter and it's coming spring 2030.

articles.title: This remarkable mod transforms the most frightening horror game of the decade into Mirror's Edge
articles.summary: Amnesia: The Bunker is without a doubt the most frightening horror game I've played this decade. Its terrifying tale of being chased through a crumbling French bunker by a monster has the darkest, thickest, most unnerving atmosphere of any horror game I've played since Alien: Isolation.
body: And yet, that's exactly what modder TiMan has done. Created for Frictional Games' 2026 modding jam —which ran with the theme of 'What is reality?'— Bunker's Edge sees the base game's protagonist Henri transported through a portal from the trenches of war-ravaged France to the pristine skyline of EA's free-running classic.

The change of scenery alone is remarkable. The Bunker's HPL engine is purpose built to deliver darkness, shadows and murk, so seeing it handle such a bright and colourful environment is mightily impressive. But what's really interesting is how TiMan has implemented all of Mirror's Edge's free-running mechanics. Mantling, sliding, wall-running, pipe-climbing, runner's vision, that 180-degree wall-jump that I always struggled to perform in the base game, it's all here.

Despite the breezier setting, Bunker's Edge is still a horror game. The Bunker's monster has followed Henri through the portal, and chases him across the rooftops just as relentlessly as it stalks him through the base game's subterranean fortification.

articles.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother Review
articles.summary: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother review: Mahershala Ali joins his would-be Blade director as a devout sword-wielding assassin.
body: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother arrives in theaters on September 25. This review is based on a screening from the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival.

Once upon a time, Oscar-winning actor Mahershala Ali was meant to play slick vampire hunter Blade for Marvel Studios under Mogul Mowgli and Bait director Bassam Tariq. The project never materialized, but it led the Muslim actor-filmmaker pair to team up for Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, a surprisingly thoughtful, action-tinged crime drama about a devout hit man trying to find breast milk for his infant daughter. This takes him through mosques and strip clubs alike in rural Virginia, laying out a visually and emotionally multifaceted journey across a heightened American landscape.

articles.title: StarCraft Devs Promise New Game Will Definitely Release in 2030
articles.summary: We got the chance to speak with the developers of the new StaCcraft game, who explained why they shared such a distant release date and even teased some potential gameplay elements.
body: StarCraft is finally getting a new game, and it’s taking a drastically different approach from its predecessors; instead of an RTS, Blizzard’s grisly sci-fi property is making its debut in the realm of open-world shooters, and it’s set to launch in 2030.

That’s a long way out from now, and it’s anyone’s guess as to what the world will look like in four years. We got the chance to ask the developers everyone’s burning question at Blizzcon 2026: Why announce the game if there’s still so much time left before it releases?
Dan Hay, GM & VP of StarCraft and AnaLee Haertling, Associate Director, told us that sharing a firm release date helps keep them “honest” — and yes, 2030 is a firm release date.
When asked if 2030 was a solid date, Hay confirmed that it is, indeed, “solid.”
points: We got the chance to speak with the developers of the new StaCcraft game, who explained why they shared such a distant release date and even teased some potential gameplay elements.

One day, he hears rumors of a mysterious dungeon said to contain incredible treasures. Every time you enter, the Mystery Dungeon takes on a new form. Items and monsters change with every expedition, and each new journey begins from Level 1. videos.summary: Raise your tattered banners in Warcrafts III’s first new campaign in over 20 years. Return to command and tear through the fields of war today, and prepare to fight alongside heroes both familiar and new in Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom.
